## bioRxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Google_Drive
This is an MCP server provided by Drive API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Drive.

CREATE TABLE "extraction_lens_links" (
    link_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    extraction_id       INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_value_extractions(extraction_id),
    -- THE THREE LENSES, typed, one per row (2026-08-28 shape; "never two lenses in one row").
    identity_code       TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_identity(identity_code),
    icf_code            TEXT REFERENCES base_icf(icf_code),
    needs_code          TEXT REFERENCES access_needs(need_code),
    -- THE WARRANT (rule 8: a judgment records its answer and its evidence in named columns).
    --   named_in_text       the figure's own words name the users / function / need (D-2)
    --   heading             the provision names no one; its heading names the group (OD-31)
    --   study_participants  a study's own participants are this group (2026-08-25 grade rule)
    --   carried             moved by migration 131 from the retired column; no judged warrant yet
    basis               TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (basis IN
                            ('named_in_text', 'heading', 'study_participants', 'carried')),
    basis_text          TEXT,          -- the exact words that warrant the link
    retired_at          TEXT,
    retired_by_session  TEXT,
    retirement_reason   TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    CHECK ((identity_code IS NOT NULL) + (icf_code IS NOT NULL)
         + (needs_code IS NOT NULL) = 1),
    CHECK ((basis = 'carried') = (basis_text IS NULL)),
    CHECK (basis_text IS NULL OR length(trim(basis_text)) > 0),
    CHECK ((retired_at IS NULL) = (retired_by_session IS NULL)
       AND (retired_at IS NULL) = (retirement_reason IS NULL))
)
---
('table', 'extraction_lens_links', 'CREATE TABLE "extraction_lens_links" (
    link_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    extraction_id       INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_value_extractions(extraction_id),

    identity_code       TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_identity(identity_code),
    icf_code            TEXT REFERENCES base_icf(icf_code),
    needs_code          TEXT REFERENCES access_needs(need_code),
    -- THE WARRANT (rule 8: a judgment records its answer and its evidence in named columns).
    --   named_in_text       the figure's own words name the users / function / need (D-2)
    --   heading             the provision names no one; its heading names the group (OD-31)
    --   study_participants  a study's own participants are this group (2026-08-25 grade rule)
    --   carried             moved by migration 131 from the retired column; no judged warrant yet
    basis               TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (basis IN
                            ('named_in_text', 'heading', 'study_participants', 'carried')),
    basis_text          TEXT,          -- the exact words that warrant the link
    retired_at          TEXT,
    retired_by_session  TEXT,
    retirement_reason   TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    CHECK ((identity_code IS NOT NULL) + (icf_code IS NOT NULL)
         + (needs_code IS NOT NULL) = 1),
    CHECK ((basis = 'carried') = (basis_text IS NULL)),
    CHECK (basis_text IS NULL OR length(trim(basis_text)) > 0),
    CHECK ((retired_at IS NULL) = (retired_by_session IS NULL)
       AND (retired_at IS NULL) = (retirement_reason IS NULL))
)')
('index', 'ux_extraction_lens_live', "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_extraction_lens_live ON extraction_lens_links
    (extraction_id, COALESCE(identity_code, ''), COALESCE(icf_code, ''),
     COALESCE(needs_code, ''))
    WHERE retired_at IS NULL")
('index', 'ix_ell_extraction', 'CREATE INDEX ix_ell_extraction ON extraction_lens_links(extraction_id)')
('index', 'ix_ell_identity', 'CREATE INDEX ix_ell_identity   ON extraction_lens_links(identity_code) WHERE retired_at IS NULL')
('index', 'ix_ell_icf', 'CREATE INDEX ix_ell_icf        ON extraction_lens_links(icf_code)      WHERE retired_at IS NULL')
('index', 'ix_ell_needs', 'CREATE INDEX ix_ell_needs      ON extraction_lens_links(needs_code)    WHERE retired_at IS NULL')
('table', 'source_value_extractions', 'CREATE TABLE "source_value_extractions" (
  extraction_id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,

  -- THE HAND-OFF KEY (D-0168; pinned by the blocking judgment_handoff_shape check):
  -- NOT NULL, a real FK at the evidence item, and NO UNIQUE index over it anywhere.
  ref_id                 TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),

  -- The slug this extraction was mined under: HISTORY. No writer sets it after migration 114 (the scan
  -- contract, LED-195: a slug guides what is searched, not what is read from a source), so it is NULL on every
  -- later row. The admission record is source_slug_links.
  slug                   TEXT REFERENCES slugs(slug),

  -- THE SUBJECT (owner 2026-08-26), now mandatory. Was nullable with `parameter` /
  -- `parameter_canonical` beside it; a NOT NULL free-text parameter NAME sitting next to
  -- a mandatory pointer at the registry that holds that same name is the dual home rule 5
  -- forbids. The name is reached: base_parameters.term_id -> terms.canonical_en.
  --
  -- AND THE VERBATIM PHRASE IS NOT LOST WITH IT. `parameter` was documented (schemas/

  -- by `db.py observe-term` and adjudicated by `adjudicate-term` (migration 068, D-0173).

  -- extraction_lens_links, read through v_live_lens_links; these four columns are held NULL by the CHECK
  -- at the foot of this table and are never written again. They are kept because committed data
  -- migrations INSERT them (CLAUDE.md rule 5: a column a committed data migration INSERTs can never be
  -- dropped). Until 131 they were real typed FKs, one per lens (owner 2026-08-28, replacing
  -- `population_code` and the free-text `population_label`), under D-0182's "at least one" CHECK.
  identity_code          TEXT REFERENCES "base_taxonomy_identity"(identity_code),
  icf_code               TEXT REFERENCES base_icf(icf_code),
  needs_code             TEXT REFERENCES access_needs(need_code),

  jurisdiction           TEXT,
  setting                TEXT,

  claim_type             TEXT NOT NULL
                           CHECK (claim_type IN ('numerical','range','qualitative','framework','absent')),
  claimed_value          TEXT,
  claimed_unit           TEXT,
  claim_text             TEXT,
  source_section         TEXT,

  -- Value genealogy / independence substrate (DR-2026-07-13 H1), carried across
  -- unchanged. v_value_independence counts distinct roots over these.
  root_id                TEXT REFERENCES external_root_registry(root_id),   -- registry-only (R24); an in-corpus root is root_ref_id
  root_type              TEXT
                           CHECK (root_type IN (
                             'measurement_primary', 'participatory_finding',
                             'committee_assertion', 'derived_calculation', 'untraced')),
  root_ref_id            TEXT REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
  echo_of                TEXT,
  measurement_paradigm   TEXT
                           CHECK (measurement_paradigm IN (
                             'swept_path_dynamic', 'static_turning_circle', 'static_clearance',
                             'anthropometric_percentile', 'instrumented_physical_measurement',
                             'route_metric', 'field_observation', 'participatory_spatial',
                             'stated_unmeasured')),
  device_class           TEXT
                           CHECK (device_class IN (
                             'manual_self_propelled', 'manual_attendant', 'power_chair', 'scooter',
                             'bariatric_manual', 'bariatric_power', 'walker_rollator',
                             'lower_limb_prosthesis', 'crutches', 'cane',
                             'mixed', 'not_device_scoped')),
  root_population_note   TEXT,
  root_classification_basis TEXT,
  contested              INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
                           CHECK (contested IN (0, 1)),
  file_anchor            TEXT,

  -- Pinpoint locator hierarchy (migration 053), carried across unchanged. These are the
  -- clause-level address that makes D-0168's 1:N fan-out legible: NBC 3.8's many clauses
  -- are many rows, and these columns are what tells them apart.
  locator_scheme         TEXT,
  loc_division           TEXT,
  loc_part               TEXT,
  loc_section            TEXT,
  loc_subsection         TEXT,
  loc_paragraph          TEXT,
  loc_clause             TEXT,
  loc_subclause          TEXT,
  loc_division_end       TEXT,
  loc_part_end           TEXT,
  loc_section_end        TEXT,
  loc_subsection_end     TEXT,
  loc_paragraph_end      TEXT,
  loc_clause_end         TEXT,
  loc_subclause_end      TEXT,
  loc_note               TEXT,

  extraction_method      TEXT NOT NULL
                           CHECK (extraction_method IN ('skim','full-read','re-read','auto-mined')),
  extraction_status      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'preliminary'
                           CHECK (extraction_status IN ('preliminary','reviewed','verified','contradicted','absent-confirmed')),
  promoted_to_rdc_id     TEXT REFERENCES reasoning_doc_citations(citation_id),
  notes                  TEXT,

  created_at             TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_by_session     TEXT,
  updated_at             TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_by_session     TEXT, figure_role TEXT
  CHECK (figure_role IS NULL OR figure_role IN ('claim', 'finding', 'condition', 'derived')), comparator TEXT

  CHECK (harm_finding = 0 OR figure_role = 'finding'), value_as_written TEXT CHECK (value_as_written IS NULL OR length(trim(value_as_written)) > 0), clause_id INTEGER REFERENCES source_clauses(clause_id),

  -- Carried across verbatim: if claim_type='absent', claimed_value must be NULL; if it

  CHECK (COALESCE(identity_code, icf_code, needs_code) IS NULL)

# A FIGURE'S LENS LIVES IN extraction_lens_links (OR-1c, migration 131): one row per (figure, code), the
# three typed columns of which a row states exactly one, and a warrant. The figure's own three columns are held
# NULL by the table's CHECK. The helpers below are the one home of what a link write checks; insert_extraction
# (every code of a new figure), add-lens-link and retire-lens-link all call them.

def _require_lens_code(conn, col: str, code: str):
    """`code` is a live key in the registry the lens column points at (a registry with no rows is named, not
    left to `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`, CLAUDE.md section 4), and a retired identity is not newly used."""
    table, key = _LENS_COLUMNS[col]
    if not dbcore.exists(conn, table, key, code):
        n = conn.execute(f'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "{table}"').fetchone()[0]
        if n == 0:
            raise Refusal(
                f"{col} {code!r}: the registry `{table}` holds no rows, so no code "
                f"is valid in this lens yet and the INSERT would fail with "
                f"`FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`. Seed the registry in a "
                f"migration, or state the value in a lens that has one.")
        raise Refusal(
            f"{col} {code!r} is not a live {key} in `{table}`. The registry is the "
            f"vocabulary (CLAUDE.md §4); it is not extended from the CLI.")
    if col == "identity_code":
        dbcore.check_identity_live(conn, code, f"{col} (a figure is not newly stated in a retired group)")


def _lens_basis_choices():
    """The warrants a writer may state: the column's own CHECK, minus `carried`, which only migration 131 writes."""
    return [v for v in (dbcore.schema_choices("extraction_lens_links", "basis") or []) if v != "carried"] or None


def _as_whole_words(text: str, field) -> bool:
    """`text` occurs in `field` on word boundaries, ignoring case (`e` is not in `the`)."""
    return bool(field) and re.search(r"(?<!\w)" + re.escape(text.lower()) + r"(?!\w)", field.lower()) is not None


def _saved_text_has(text: str, ref_id: str) -> bool:
    """`text` is in a file saved FOR `ref_id` (a scoped hit; a hit in another source's file proves nothing)."""
    return _retrieval_log().locate_quote(text, ref_id=ref_id)[0] == "scoped"


def _require_lens_warrant(conn, basis, basis_text, ref_id, claim_text, source_section, context):
    """A link's warrant: a basis from the column's own CHECK (not `carried`) and the exact words that warrant it,
    which must be found on word boundaries, in the place the basis names:

      named_in_text       the figure's claim_text, or a file saved for its source (D-2: its own words name the users);
      heading             the figure's source_section, its own heading (OD-31);
      study_participants  the study_population of an evidence_population_match row for the source (2026-08-25).

    Returns the stripped text. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHECK: that the words name the lens code itself. The registries
    do not hold a name for every code (about half the ICF d-codes have no title, access_needs has no name column), so a name test cannot be derived for them; whether the words name the group
    is the judge's (D-2) and the recorded warrant is what a later reader audits."""
    allowed = set(_lens_basis_choices() or ())
    if basis not in allowed:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{context}: a lens link needs --lens-basis / --basis, one of {sorted(allowed)} (the warrant for "
            f"stating the figure in this group). Nothing was written.")
    text = (basis_text or "").strip()
    if not text:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{context}: the warrant's words are blank. Give --lens-basis-text / --basis-text: the exact words "
            f"of the figure, its heading or its study's participants that name the group. Nothing was written.")
    if not re.search(r"\w", text):
        raise Refusal(f"{context}: the warrant {text!r} holds no letter or digit, so it names no one. "
                      f"Nothing was written.")
    if basis == "named_in_text":
        where = f"the figure's claim_text, or a file saved for {ref_id}"
        found = _as_whole_words(text, claim_text) or _saved_text_has(text, ref_id)
    elif basis == "heading":
        where = "the figure's source_section (its heading)"
        found = _as_whole_words(text, source_section)
    else:
        where = f"the study_population of an evidence_population_match row for {ref_id}"
        found = any(_as_whole_words(text, r[0]) for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT study_population FROM evidence_population_match WHERE source_ref=?", (ref_id,)))
    if not found:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{context}: the warrant {text!r} (basis {basis}) is not, on word boundaries, in {where}. A link "
            f"rests on words the source holds, never on memory (CLAUDE.md 5(c)); a basis names where to look: "
            f"named_in_text the claim text or the source's saved file, heading the source_section, "
            f"study_participants the graded study_population. Nothing was written.")
    return text


def _write_lens_link(conn, extraction_id: int, col: str, code: str, basis: str, basis_text, session: str) -> int:
    """INSERT one live link and return its link_id. The caller has checked the code and the warrant."""
    row = {"extraction_id": extraction_id, col: code, "basis": basis, "basis_text": basis_text,
           **dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "extraction_lens_links", session)}
    return conn.execute(
        f"INSERT INTO extraction_lens_links ({','.join(row)}) VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(row))})",
        list(row.values())).lastrowid

def insert_extraction(data: dict, session: str, dry_run: bool = False,
                      relations: list = None, verbatim_exempt: str = None):
    """Record ONE judgment item: what one source asserts for one parameter.

    THE WRITER THIS TABLE SHIPPED WITHOUT. `source_value_extractions` has existed
    since migration 018 and `scripts/db.py` contained ZERO references to it —
    measured 2026-09-10, `grep -c source_value_extractions scripts/db.py` -> 0. With
    no extraction writer there was no parameter->evidence edge at all, so the
    determination engine had nothing to gather evidence by except the slug, and
    `param 1 x MOB -> stated` meant "everything linked to
    accessible-circulation-geometry" — 10 sources, 8 of which the engine's own report
    flagged `tier_inconsistent`. This function is what makes that join exist.

    WHAT IT REFUSES, and why each refusal is the point:

    * An unknown `ref_id`. The FK would say `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`, which
      names neither the source nor the fix. An extraction is a reading OF a source;
      one that names no admitted source is a claim about nothing.

    * A `root_id` the registry does not hold (`external_root_registry`; migration 114).

    * A MISSING OR BLANK `claim_text`. Migration 073 retired `parameter`, the last
      NOT NULL column carrying the source's own words; `claim_text`,
      `source_section` and all 16 `loc_*` columns are nullable, so without this the
      happy path writes a row with ZERO verbatim from the source it read. The
      guarantee is the CLI's, not the schema's — say so rather than implying the
      table enforces it.

    * EXCEPT for `figure_role='derived'` (T-063, OD-40): a derived row stores NO claim_text (one given is refused;
      a figure a source states in words is a claim row) and, with no locator of its own, is checked for one on each
      `derived_from` input instead of R3's two refusals. Its words and its place are its inputs'.

    * A `parameter_id` that is absent, or whose row is not `status='active'`. A
      determination keyed on a parameter folded into another is a determination about
      a subject that no longer stands on its own, and the FK cannot see the
      difference because the row is still there. `assess_cell.validate_parameter()`
      refuses the same thing at the other end; both ends refuse or neither does.

    * FK-INTO-EMPTY-PARENT, refused EARLY and by name. `base_parameters` holds 0 rows
      today, so a bare INSERT dies with `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` at INSERT and
      never at migration time — the exact failure CLAUDE.md §4 says "makes a broken
      table look healthy": the schema parses, a rebuild reproduces it exactly, and
      every gate stays green over a table that cannot accept a row. The refusal here
      names `db.py add-parameter` as the remedy. The same treatment is given to each
      lens registry.

    * A lens code that is not live in its own registry — and a BLANK is not an
      absence. `--identity ""` is normalised to None before anything reads it:
      assess_cell records the live incident where a blank skipped validation (falsy),
      satisfied the at-least-one test at the NEXT lens (truthy), was INSERTed as '',
      and produced a `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` violation against `populations`.

    * NO LENS AT ALL. D-0182: absence in a lens is fine, absence in all four is not.
      A value attached to no lens is a value about nobody. Since migration 131 (OR-1c) the lens
      is a set of LINKS, not the figure's four columns (held NULL): each lens key of `data`
      takes one code or a list, `lens_basis` / `lens_basis_text` (not columns) are the warrant of
      every link the call writes, and the figure and its links land in one transaction.

    * The claim/value contradiction, IN WORDS. The table's own CHECK already refuses
      `claim_type='absent'` with a value and any other claim_type without one; this
      refuses it first so the operator gets a sentence instead of
      "CHECK constraint failed", which names neither column.

    * Any value outside a column's own declared CHECK vocabulary, for all six
      vocabulary columns, read from the schema and never from a list in code.

    DELIBERATELY ABSENT REFUSALS — each must STAY absent, and this is where the next
    reader is told so rather than discovering it by removing one:

    * NO UNIQUENESS ON (ref_id, parameter_id). This is the ruled 1:N fan-out. D-0168
      (owner, 2026-08-27): "one evidence source may provide many rows of judgment (eg
      a code document like Canada's NBC 3.8)" — many clauses, many rows, one source,
      one parameter. It is ALSO the DR-2026-08-19 §7 dissent contest: a divergent
      adversarial grade lands as a SECOND row and divergent readings are meant to be
      readable as a contest, not silently overwritten. A uniqueness refusal here
      would be the CLI quietly overruling doctrine, and
      `scripts/audit/judgment_handoff_shape.py` (BLOCKING) fails if the same
      collapse is attempted in the schema. A duplicate is NOTED on stderr, never
      refused: if it is unintended the author sees it in the same session; if it is
      intended it is the whole point.

    * NO VALUE-DIRECTNESS GRADE. There is no value-directness grading rule in this
      repository (workplan 2026-09-10, stop condition 4: "Any step needing a
      value-directness grading rule. None exists. Do not invent one."). The engine
      records the dimension NOT_ASSESSED under G2 — applies but unassessed, never
      silently EXACT. Accepting a grade here would be inventing the rule at the
      point of capture, where it is least visible.

    * NO `--promoted-to-rdc-id`. Promotion to the synthesis layer is a later act on
      an existing row with its own verdict behind it (rule #10 re-read). Letting
      capture assert it would mint an extraction that claims to have been verified
      before it was read twice.

    ADDED 2026-09-13 BY MIGRATION 075's WRITER, and refused the same way as
    everything above: `--figure-role` (REQUIRED -- a value with no role reads as a
    claim), `--comparator`, and `relations` -- a list of edge dicts written into
    `extraction_relations` in this SAME transaction (the `add-term` precedent: a
    term and its adjudication land together, and here a figure and what it is
    stated relative to do too). `--relation` is REQUIRED at the CLI; the literal
    'none' (which arrives here as `relations == []`) says the source states its
    figure absolutely. See `_write_relation_edge` for the edge-level refusals and
    `_build_relation_groups` for how the CLI's repeatable flags become this list.
    """
    _COLS = frozenset({
        "ref_id", "parameter_id",
        "jurisdiction", "setting",
        "claim_type", "claimed_value", "claimed_unit", "claim_text", "source_section",
        "root_id", "root_type", "root_ref_id", "echo_of", "measurement_paradigm",
        "device_class", "root_population_note", "root_classification_basis",
        "contested", "file_anchor",
        "locator_scheme", "loc_division", "loc_part", "loc_section", "loc_subsection",
        "loc_paragraph", "loc_clause", "loc_subclause",
        "loc_division_end", "loc_part_end", "loc_section_end", "loc_subsection_end",
        "loc_paragraph_end", "loc_clause_end", "loc_subclause_end", "loc_note", "clause_id",
        "extraction_method", "extraction_status", "notes",
        "figure_role", "comparator", "harm_finding", "value_as_written",
    })
    # THE LENS KEYS AND THE WARRANT ARE NOT COLUMNS OF THE FIGURE (migration 131): they become its links.
    # A key takes one code or a list; a BLANK IS NOT AN ABSENCE, so a blank code is dropped before
    # anything reads it.
    data = dict(data)
    lens_basis, lens_basis_text = data.pop("lens_basis", None), data.pop("lens_basis_text", None)
    lens = {}
    for col in _LENS_COLUMNS:
        given = data.pop(col, None)
        given = [given] if isinstance(given, str) else given
        if given is not None and (not isinstance(given, (list, tuple)) or not all(
                c is None or isinstance(c, str) for c in given)):
            raise Refusal(f"{col}: a code is text, or a list of text codes; got {given!r}. Nothing was written.")
        lens[col] = [c.strip() for c in (given or ()) if c is not None and c.strip()]
    dbcore.validate_cols(data.keys(), _COLS, "insert_extraction")
    dbcore.check_jurisdiction(data.get("jurisdiction"), "add-extraction --jurisdiction")
    row = {k: v for k, v in data.items() if v is not None}

    # A BLANK IS NOT AN ABSENCE — normalise before anything reads these.
    for col in ("value_as_written",):
        if col in row and not str(row[col]).strip():
            del row[col]
    if "value_as_written" in row:
        row["value_as_written"] = str(row["value_as_written"]).strip()

    with dbcore.connect(dry_run) as conn:
        ref = dbcore.fold_ref(row.get("ref_id"))
        if not dbcore.exists(conn, "evidence_sources", "ref_id", ref):
            raise Refusal(
                f"ref_id {data.get('ref_id')!r} is not an admitted source. An extraction "
                f"is a reading OF a source; extract AFTER admission.\n"
                f"  db.py add-source ...")
        _refuse_tombstone(conn, ref, "add-extraction")
        row["ref_id"] = ref
        # AN EXTRACTION IS A READING. A source whose existence is not established
        # (verification_status UNVERIFIED or NULL, D-0157) was never obtained, and the
        # skill says never to describe it as read; a value attributed to it is a claim
        # about a document nobody held. Live rows already sit on such sources (derive:
        # SELECT COUNT(*) FROM source_value_extractions x JOIN evidence_sources e USING
        # (ref_id) WHERE COALESCE(e.verification_status,'') <> 'VERIFIED'); they are
        # history, and this refusal stops the next one.
        _vs = conn.execute("SELECT verification_status FROM evidence_sources WHERE ref_id=?",
                           (ref,)).fetchone()[0]
        if _vs != "VERIFIED":
            raise Refusal(
                f"add-extraction: {ref} is {_vs or 'NULL'}, not VERIFIED. An extraction is a "
                f"reading of a document this project obtained; a source whose standing is "
                f"not established cannot have been read. Retrieve and verify it first "
                f"(R10; db.py amend-source), or admit it UNVERIFIED and leave it unread. "
                f"Nothing was written.")

        # A slug guides what is searched, not what is read (scan contract, LED-195): no slug is
        # asked for here, and `source_slug_links` stays the admission record. A root_id names a
        # row of the registry (migration 114); an in-corpus root is root_ref_id.
        if row.get("root_id") is not None and not dbcore.exists(
                conn, "external_root_registry", "root_id", row["root_id"]):
            raise Refusal(
                f"root_id {row['root_id']!r} is not in external_root_registry. A root_id names an "
                f"external root; a root held in this corpus is --root-ref-id. Register the root "
                f"first with `db.py register-root`, then give its id here.")

        # --- the subject -----------------------------------------------------
        pid = row.get("parameter_id")
        if pid is None:
            raise Refusal(
                "--parameter-id is required: an extraction whose subject is unknown "
                "cannot reach the determination it exists to support (owner 2026-08-26, "
                "'the judgment object is the canonical parameter').")
        n_params = conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM base_parameters").fetchone()[0]
        if n_params == 0:
            raise Refusal(
                "`base_parameters` holds no rows, so NO parameter_id can be valid and a "
                "bare INSERT would fail with `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` — a refusal "
                "that names neither the cause nor the fix (CLAUDE.md §4).\n"
                "Mint the subject first, from an adjudicated term:\n"
                "  db.py add-parameter --term-id TERM-NNN --quantity-kind K --quantity-kind-quote Q --quantity-kind-source-url U --quantity-kind-source-page P --session ...")
        prow = conn.execute("SELECT status, merged_into FROM base_parameters "
                            "WHERE parameter_id=?", (pid,)).fetchone()
        if prow is None:
            raise Refusal(
                f"parameter_id {pid}: no such parameter. Mint one from a term:\n"
                f"  db.py add-parameter --term-id TERM-NNN --quantity-kind K --quantity-kind-quote Q --quantity-kind-source-url U --quantity-kind-source-page P --session ...")
        if prow["status"] != "active":
            target = f" (merged into {prow['merged_into']})" if prow["merged_into"] else ""
            raise Refusal(
                f"parameter_id {pid} is {prow['status']}{target}, not active. Key the "
                f"extraction on the surviving parameter — a value filed under a folded "
                f"parameter is unreachable from the determination that replaced it.")

        # --- the reading record (R16, OR-11a) --------------------------------
        # The reading comes first and leaves a source_scans row; what it found is this
        # row. An extraction with no covering reading is consumed before it was read
        # (adversarial lens S4-sequence). `verified` additionally needs the reading to
        # be full-scope (OR-11a, owner 2026-10-29). Both were stated by the skill and
        # held by nothing; the live rows that lack a covering reading are history (derive
        # the verified ones: python3 scripts/audit/verified_scan_integrity.py).
        if _covering_scan(conn, ref, pid) is None:
            raise Refusal(
                f"add-extraction: no source_scans row covers {ref} for parameter {pid}. "
                f"Record the reading first -- db.py record-scan --ref-id {ref} --mode "
                f"catalogue (or --mode targeted --target-parameter-id {pid}) -- then "
                f"write what it found. Nothing was written.")
        if row.get("extraction_status") == "verified":
            _require_full_scan_for_verified(conn, ref, pid, "add-extraction")

        # --- the lenses ------------------------------------------------------
        if not any(lens.values()):
            raise Refusal(
                "an extraction must be stated in at least one lens (D-0182): pass one or "
                "more of --identity / --icf / --needs. A value attached to no "
                "lens is a value about nobody.")
        for col, codes in lens.items():
            dup = sorted({c for c in codes if codes.count(c) > 1})
            if dup:
                raise Refusal(f"{col}: {dup} given more than once in this call. A figure holds one live "
                              f"link per code. Nothing was written.")
            for code in codes:
                _require_lens_code(conn, col, code)

        # --- the claim -------------------------------------------------------
        claim_type = row.get("claim_type")
        value = row.get("claimed_value")
        figure_role = row.get("figure_role")
        # A DERIVED FIGURE HAS NO QUOTE OR LOCATOR OF ITS OWN (OD-40, delegated 2026-11-13): its words and its
        # place are its inputs', reached through its `derived_from` edges, each of which carries its input's
        # verified quote. A figure a source states in words is a claim row, never a derived one.
        if figure_role == "derived":
            if "claim_text" in row:
                raise Refusal(
                    "add-extraction: a derived figure carries no claim_text of its own: its words are its inputs', "
                    "reached through its derived_from edges (OD-40). A figure the source states in words is a claim "
                    "row (--figure-role claim); a computed one is written with db.py derive-extraction. "
                    "Nothing was written.")
        # THE VERBATIM FLOOR. `--claim-text` is required at the parser, so this fires
        # on the PYTHON API path and on `--claim-text ""` — a blank is not a quote,
        # and normalising it to None here would restore exactly the zero-verbatim row
        # the requirement exists to forbid.
        elif not str(row.get("claim_text") or "").strip():
            raise Refusal(
                "--claim-text is required and must not be blank. Migration 073 retired "
                "`parameter`, the last NOT NULL column that carried the source's own "
                "words; every remaining verbatim column on this table is nullable, so "
                "without --claim-text this row would assert a value with nothing of the "
                "source's own phrasing behind it. Quote the clause you read.")

        # THE QUOTE MUST BE IN THE BYTES (CLAUDE.md 5(c), added 2026-09-13). Blank was
        # the ONLY thing refused above; the sentence a determination rests on could be
        # composed from memory and nothing looked. Demonstrated during the audit:
        # claimed_value 9999 with an invented claim_text landed and governed a cell.
        # `--verbatim-exempt` is the ledgered escape for text no artefact can carry, and
        # is itself refused when the text would have verified.
        if figure_role != "derived":
            _exempt_note = _require_verbatim(
                str(row["claim_text"]), row.get("ref_id"), "--claim-text",
                "add-extraction", exempt_reason=verbatim_exempt, claimed_value=value,
                claim_type=claim_type, value_as_written=row.get("value_as_written"))
            if _exempt_note:
                row["notes"] = ((row.get("notes") or "") + " " + _exempt_note).strip()

        # THE LENS WARRANT: the words that name the group are the figure's own (or its source's).
        lens_basis_text = _require_lens_warrant(
            conn, lens_basis, lens_basis_text, ref, row.get("claim_text"), row.get("source_section"),
            "add-extraction")

        # THE CLAUSE (T-031, OD-23). A figure read from an inventoried clause points at its source_clauses row, and
        # its locator is reached through that pointer (rule 5): any locator field beside it (_sve_locator_fields) is
        # a second home, refused; so is a clause another source's reading recorded, and a quote that is not inside
        # the clause's text (the one matching rule, retrieval_log.normalise_quote). R3 below reads the pointer through
        # dbcore.clause_pinpoint_sql.
        if row.get("clause_id") is not None:
            _cl = conn.execute("SELECT s.ref_id, c.clause_text FROM source_clauses c JOIN source_scans s "
                               "ON s.scan_id = c.scan_id WHERE c.clause_id = ?", (row["clause_id"],)).fetchone()
            if _cl is None:
                raise Refusal(f"add-extraction: --clause-id {row['clause_id']} is not a clause of the inventory "
                              f"(source_clauses). Nothing was written.")
            if _cl[0] != ref:
                raise Refusal(f"add-extraction: clause {row['clause_id']} is a clause of {_cl[0]}, not of {ref}. "
                              f"Nothing was written.")
            _typed = sorted(c for c in row if c in _sve_locator_fields())
            if _typed:
                raise Refusal(f"add-extraction: --clause-id reaches the locator through the clause row, so "
                              f"{', '.join('--' + c.replace('_', '-') for c in _typed)} would write it a second "
                              f"time (CLAUDE.md rule 5). Drop them. Nothing was written.")
            _nq = _retrieval_log().normalise_quote(str(row.get("claim_text") or ""))
            if not _nq or _nq not in _retrieval_log().normalise_quote(_cl[1]):

raise Refusal(f"add-extraction: {_why}. Nothing was written.")

        # --- the relation edges (migration 075's extraction_relations) --------
        # REQUIRED, and checked here rather than only at the parser so the PYTHON
        # API path refuses too -- the same discipline --claim-text already gets.
        if relations is None:
            raise Refusal(
                "--relation is required: pass the literal 'none' (source states "
                "its figure absolutely) or one or more real relation edges. Five "
                "of five corridor-width sources in the live corpus state theirs "
                "against a reference they name or invoke -- silence is not "
                "'absolute', it is unchecked.")
        if figure_role == "derived":
            _have = {e.get("input_role") for e in relations if e.get("relation") == "derived_from"}
            if not {"base", "delta"} <= _have:
                raise Refusal(
                    "figure_role='derived' requires a derived_from edge carrying --input-role base AND one "
                    "carrying --input-role delta (db.py derive-extraction writes both). A derived row with nothing "
                    "pointing at what it was computed FROM, or with one input, is a number trusted on faith, "
                    "which is exactly what v_derived_figure_check (migration 075) exists to stop trusting "
                    "silently. Nothing was written.")
            if claim_type != "numerical":
                raise Refusal("figure_role='derived' is a computed number: --claim-type must be 'numerical'. "
                              "A sentence a source states is a claim row. Nothing was written.")

        # A BYTE-IDENTICAL ROW IS A COPY, NOT A CONTEST. D-0168 protects a DIVERGENT second
        # reading; a row equal in every column the source supplied adds nothing a reader
        # could weigh and would count twice in anything that counts rows. Refused by the
        # same measure _write_relation_edge uses for an edge. Session and status columns are
        # not compared: the same reading by a second session is still the same reading.
        _same_cols = [c for c in row
                      if c not in ("notes", "extraction_status", "extraction_method", "contested")]
        _keyed = ("claimed_value", "claimed_unit", "source_section", "loc_section", "loc_clause")
        _preds = [f'"{c}" IS ?' for c in _same_cols] + [f'"{c}" IS NULL' for c in _keyed
                                                        if c not in row]
        # THE LENS IS NOT PART OF THE ROW'S IDENTITY (migration 131): a figure is written once and stated in
        # each group by a link, so the same reading in another group is `add-lens-link`, never a second figure
        # (a second copy would count the one reading twice).
        _dups = conn.execute(
            "SELECT extraction_id FROM source_value_extractions WHERE " + " AND ".join(_preds),
            [row[c] for c in _same_cols]).fetchall()
        if figure_role == "derived":
            # A derived row has no words of its own to tell two derivations apart, so what makes it a copy is the
            # same inputs in the same roles: 5.5 + 9.25 and 10 + 4.75 are two derivations of one result.
            _mine = {(e.get("to_extraction"), e.get("input_role")) for e in relations if e.get("relation") == "derived_from"}
            _dups = [d for d in _dups if {(r[0], r[1]) for r in conn.execute(
                "SELECT to_extraction_id, input_role FROM extraction_relations WHERE from_extraction_id=? "
                "AND relation='derived_from'", (d[0],))} == _mine]
        _dup = _dups[0] if _dups else None
        if _dup:
            raise Refusal(
                f"add-extraction: extraction {_dup[0]} already carries this exact row "
                f"({ref}, parameter {pid}, claim, value, text and locator; the lens is not part of a "
                f"figure's identity). A byte-identical copy is not a second reading; a divergent one is "
                f"(D-0168). To state the same figure in another lens code use: db.py add-lens-link "
                f"--extraction-id {_dup[0]} ... Nothing was written.")

        # DELIBERATELY NOT REFUSED — see the docstring. Noted so the fan-out is
        # visible in the session log rather than silent.
        prior = conn.execute(
            "SELECT extraction_id, created_by_session FROM source_value_extractions "
            "WHERE ref_id=? AND parameter_id=?", (ref, pid)).fetchall()
        if prior:
            print(f"NOTE: {ref} already carries {len(prior)} extraction(s) for parameter "
                  f"{pid} ({[r[0] for r in prior]}). Writing another — evidence to "
                  f"judgment is 1:N (D-0168), and a divergent reading is a contest "
                  f"(DR-2026-08-19 §7), not an error.", file=sys.stderr)

        row.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "source_value_extractions", session))
        cur = conn.execute(
            f"INSERT INTO source_value_extractions ({','.join(row)}) "
            f"VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(row))})", list(row.values()))
        extraction_id = cur.lastrowid
        links = [{"link_id": _write_lens_link(conn, extraction_id, col, code, lens_basis, lens_basis_text,
                                              session), "lens": col, "code": code}
                 for col, codes in lens.items() for code in codes]

        # THE EDGES, IN THIS SAME TRANSACTION -- the `add-term` precedent (a term
        # and its adjudication land together). `relations` is `[]` for the literal
        # 'none' (source states its figure absolutely) and a list of edge dicts
        # otherwise; every refusal for an individual edge lives in
        # _write_relation_edge so there is one copy of that logic, not one per
        # caller (add-extraction / relate-extraction / derive-extraction).
        relation_ids = []
        for edge in relations:
            relation_ids.append(_write_relation_edge(
                conn, verbatim_exempt=verbatim_exempt,
                from_id=extraction_id, from_ref_id=ref,
                from_figure_role=figure_role, from_comparator=row.get("comparator"),
                relation=edge.get("relation"), to_extraction=edge.get("to_extraction"),
                to_label=edge.get("to_label"), to_kind=edge.get("to_kind"),
                stated=edge.get("stated"), quote=edge.get("quote"),
                input_role=edge.get("input_role"), notes=edge.get("notes"),
                cross_source_reason=edge.get("cross_source_reason"),
                session=session, context="add-extraction"))
        if figure_role == "derived":
            _refuse_derived_mismatch(conn, extraction_id, "add-extraction")

        return {"extraction_id": extraction_id, "ref_id": ref, "parameter_id": pid,
                "lens": links,
                "claim_type": claim_type, "claimed_value": value,
                "figure_role": figure_role, "comparator": row.get("comparator"),
                "relation_ids": relation_ids,
                "siblings_for_this_parameter": len(prior),
                "dry_run": dry_run}


def add_lens_link(extraction_id: int, session: str, *, identity: str = None, icf: str = None,
                  needs: str = None, basis: str = None, basis_text: str = None,
                  dry_run: bool = False):
    """State an existing figure in ONE more lens code (OR-1c), with the words that warrant it.

    Refuses: a figure that does not exist; none or more than one code; a code the registry lacks or a
    retired identity (`_require_lens_code`); a missing basis, a blank or unfound warrant
    (`_require_lens_warrant`); a live link already holding the code, EXCEPT a `carried` one, which is
    retired in this same transaction ("superseded by judged link <id>") because a judged warrant
    replaces a carried one in one act. The retirement is written first and its reason completed once
    the new link has an id: the partial unique index admits one live link per (figure, code)."""
    given = {col: code for col, code in (("identity_code", identity), ("icf_code", icf),
                                         ("needs_code", needs))
             if code is not None}
    if len(given) != 1:
        raise Refusal(f"add-lens-link: name exactly one code, with one of --identity / --icf / --needs "
                      f"(got {len(given)}). Repeat the verb for each code. Nothing was written.")
    ((col, code),) = given.items()
    if not isinstance(code, str):
        raise Refusal(f"add-lens-link: {col} must be one code as text, got {code!r}. Nothing was written.")
    with dbcore.connect(dry_run) as conn:
        fig = conn.execute(
            "SELECT ref_id, claim_text, source_section "
            "FROM source_value_extractions WHERE extraction_id=?", (extraction_id,)).fetchone()
        if fig is None:
            raise Refusal(f"add-lens-link: extraction {extraction_id}: no such figure. Nothing was written.")
        _require_lens_code(conn, col, code)
        text = _require_lens_warrant(conn, basis, basis_text, fig["ref_id"], fig["claim_text"],
                                     fig["source_section"], "add-lens-link")
        held = conn.execute(
            f"SELECT link_id, basis FROM extraction_lens_links WHERE extraction_id=? AND {col}=? "
            f"AND retired_at IS NULL", (extraction_id, code)).fetchone()
        if held is not None and held["basis"] != "carried":
            raise Refusal(
                f"add-lens-link: extraction {extraction_id} already holds a live {held['basis']} link "
                f"({held['link_id']}) for {col} {code!r}. A figure holds one live link per code; retire it "
                f"first (retire-lens-link) if its warrant is wrong. Nothing was written.")
        if held is not None:
            conn.execute(
                "UPDATE extraction_lens_links SET retired_at=?, retired_by_session=?, retirement_reason=?, "
                "updated_at=?, updated_by_session=? WHERE link_id=?",
                [dbcore.now(), dbcore.session_stem(session), "superseded by judged link", dbcore.now(),
                 dbcore.session_stem(session), held["link_id"]])
        link_id = _write_lens_link(conn, extraction_id, col, code, basis, text, session)
        if held is not None:
            conn.execute("UPDATE extraction_lens_links SET retirement_reason=? WHERE link_id=?",
                         (f"superseded by judged link {link_id}", held["link_id"]))

                "dry_run": dry_run}


def retire_lens_link(link_id: int, reason: str, session: str, dry_run: bool = False):
    """Retire one lens link in place (OD-29): the three retired_* columns and the updated_* pair.

    Refuses: no such link; already retired; a blank reason; and the figure's LAST live link, because a
    figure with no lens is a value about nobody (D-0182) and the schema no longer holds that rule."""
    with dbcore.connect(dry_run) as conn:
        link = conn.execute("SELECT extraction_id, retired_at FROM extraction_lens_links WHERE link_id=?",
                            (link_id,)).fetchone()
        if link is None:
            raise Refusal(f"retire-lens-link: link {link_id}: no such link. Nothing was written.")
        if link["retired_at"] is not None:
            raise Refusal(f"retire-lens-link: link {link_id} was retired at {link['retired_at']}. "
                          f"Nothing was written.")
        if not (reason or "").strip():
            raise Refusal("retire-lens-link: --reason is blank. Say why the figure is no longer stated "
                          "in this group. Nothing was written.")
        if conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM v_live_lens_links WHERE extraction_id=?",
                        (link["extraction_id"],)).fetchone()[0] == 1:
            raise Refusal(
                f"retire-lens-link: link {link_id} is extraction {link['extraction_id']}'s last live link. "
                f"Add the replacing link first with add-lens-link; a figure with no lens is a value about "
                f"nobody (D-0182). Nothing was written.")
        conn.execute(
            "UPDATE extraction_lens_links SET retired_at=?, retired_by_session=?, retirement_reason=?, "
            "updated_at=?, updated_by_session=? WHERE link_id=?",
            [dbcore.now(), dbcore.session_stem(session), reason.strip(), dbcore.now(),
             dbcore.session_stem(session), link_id])
        return {"link_id": link_id, "extraction_id": link["extraction_id"], "retired": True,
                "dry_run": dry_run}

def derive_extraction(*, ref_id: str = None, parameter_id: int, base: int,
                      delta: int, session: str,
                      dry_run: bool = False, identity: str = None, icf: str = None,
                      needs: str = None,
                      lens_basis: str = None, lens_basis_text: str = None,
                      claimed_value: str = None):
    """Write a figure_role='derived' row computed as base + delta, plus the two
    derived_from edges `v_derived_figure_check` (migration 075) re-verifies it
    against -- a derived figure is never a number trusted on faith.

    Reads --base/--delta with a READ-ONLY pass first (their claimed_value/unit are
    needed to compute or check this row's own before `insert_extraction` can be
    called at all); the actual WRITE -- the row and both derived_from edges -- is
    the ONE transaction inside that single `insert_extraction` call, the same
    guarantee every other caller of it gets.

    WHAT IT DERIVES, and what it never asks for (T-063, OD-40): the comparator (`_derived_comparator`) and the
    unit are the inputs' (two inputs in two units are refused: no check recomputes a converted figure); the quote
    and the locator are the inputs' too, reached through the two edges, each of which carries its input's quote.
    A derived row stores neither; it is refused when an input lacks a quote or a locator. `ref_id` is NOT NULL, so
    it is a POINTER to the base input's source (as `root_ref_id` is), not an attribution of the figure to it.
    The refusals reached through it carry the prefix `add-extraction:` (the writer is shared).
    """
    with dbcore.connect(dry_run, readonly=True) as conn:
        cols = "*"
        base_row = conn.execute(f"SELECT {cols} FROM source_value_extractions WHERE extraction_id=?", (base,)).fetchone()
        if base_row is None:
            raise Refusal(
                f"derive-extraction: --base {base}: no such extraction. A derived "
                f"figure is computed from a row this project actually holds, never "
                f"invented -- extract the base figure first with add-extraction.")
        delta_row = conn.execute(f"SELECT {cols} FROM source_value_extractions WHERE extraction_id=?", (delta,)).fetchone()
        if delta_row is None:
            raise Refusal(
                f"derive-extraction: --delta {delta}: no such extraction. Extract "
                f"the delta figure first with add-extraction.")
        if base == delta:
            raise Refusal("derive-extraction: --base and --delta must be different "
                          "rows -- a figure cannot be derived from itself twice.")
        for _id, _row in ((base, base_row), (delta, delta_row)):
            _refuse_bad_derived_input(conn, "derive-extraction", _row)
        if base_row["ref_id"] != delta_row["ref_id"]:
            raise Refusal(
                f"derive-extraction: base {base} is from {base_row['ref_id']} and delta {delta} from "
                f"{delta_row['ref_id']}. This verb adds figures ONE source states; a derivation across two documents "
                f"is a synthesis act this verb does not write. Nothing was written.")
        if ref_id is not None and ref_id != base_row["ref_id"]:
            raise Refusal(
                f"derive-extraction: --ref-id {ref_id} is not the inputs' source ({base_row['ref_id']}); the "
                f"derived row is filed under its inputs' source and the flag is only a check. Omit it. "
                f"Nothing was written.")
        ref_id = base_row["ref_id"]

        base_unit, delta_unit = base_row["claimed_unit"], delta_row["claimed_unit"]
        if base_unit != delta_unit:
            raise Refusal(
                f"derive-extraction: base {base} is stated in {base_unit!r} and delta {delta} in {delta_unit!r}. "
                f"This verb adds figures stated in one unit; a converted figure is not recomputed by any check "
                f"(v_derived_figure_check joins on equal units). Nothing was written.")
        comparator = _derived_comparator(base_row["comparator"], delta_row["comparator"])
        if comparator is None:
            raise Refusal(
                f"derive-extraction: the sum of base {base} ({base_row['comparator'] or 'no comparator'}) and delta "
                f"{delta} ({delta_row['comparator'] or 'no comparator'}) is not a bound. A point delta ('=') moves "
                f"the base's bound; two bounds of the same kind add. Set a missing comparator with "
                f"amend-extraction --field comparator. Nothing was written.")

        def _num(x):
            try:
                return float(x)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                return None
        bn, dn = _num(base_row["claimed_value"]), _num(delta_row["claimed_value"])
        if bn is None or dn is None or base_unit is None:
            raise Refusal(
                f"derive-extraction: base {base} ({base_row['claimed_value']!r} {base_unit!r}) and delta {delta} "
                f"({delta_row['claimed_value']!r} {delta_unit!r}) cannot be summed: both must be plain numerals in "
                f"one stated unit (a ratio, a range or a figure with no unit is not added, and no check could "
                f"recompute it, v_derived_figure_check). Nothing was written.")
        # A supplied --claimed-value is compared with base + delta by `_refuse_derived_mismatch`
        # (the one home of that arithmetic), inside `insert_extraction`'s transaction.
        if claimed_value is None:
            claimed_value = _fmt_num(bn + dn)

        data = {"ref_id": ref_id, "parameter_id": parameter_id,
                "identity_code": identity, "icf_code": icf, "needs_code": needs,
                "lens_basis": lens_basis,
                "lens_basis_text": lens_basis_text, "claim_type": "numerical",
                "claimed_value": claimed_value, "claimed_unit": base_unit,
                "figure_role": "derived",
                "comparator": comparator, "extraction_method": "auto-mined",
                "root_type": "derived_calculation", "root_ref_id": base_row["ref_id"]}
        # EACH EDGE CARRIES ITS OWN TARGET'S QUOTE, not this row's (a derived row has none: OD-40).
        # Every edge quote is checked as a byte-substring of a persisted retrieval artefact. The base and
        # delta rows' own claim_text values already passed that check when those rows were written, so using
        # them is an APPLICATION of the rule rather than a carve-out from it -- and it is also the truer
        # record: the warrant for "this figure derives from that one" is what that one says. (Corrected
        # 2026-09-13: passing the analyst's computation statement as both edge quotes made this verb
        # structurally unable to succeed, which is worse than a missing verb because it looks implemented;
        # T-063 then removed that statement, the locator and the comparator it also lacked.)
        relations = [
            {"relation": "derived_from", "to_extraction": base, "stated": "named",
             "quote": base_row["claim_text"], "input_role": "base"},
            {"relation": "derived_from", "to_extraction": delta, "stated": "named",
             "quote": delta_row["claim_text"], "input_role": "delta"},
        ]
    return insert_extraction(data, session=session, dry_run=dry_run,
                             relations=relations)

    record("M01", "log-search refuses an unknown lens code on each of the three flags and writes nothing",
           all(rc != 0 and named for rc, named in refused.values()) and counts("search_executions") == n_before,
           f"{refused} rows {n_before} -> {counts('search_executions')}")
    r = ls_lens("live codes", *[x for kv in lens_live.items() for x in kv])
    row = q("SELECT identity_code, icf_code, needs_code FROM search_executions "
            "WHERE query_text=?", "fixture M: live codes")

    import importlib                                               # noqa: E402

           and ("'%s', '%s', '%s', NULL" % (lens_live["--identity"], lens_live["--icf"], lens_live["--needs"])) in ln]
    record("M03", "emit_batch_sql captures the lens columns of a logged search (the write can be shipped)",
           len(hit) == 1, captured[-400:])

                       "--prior-expectation", "fixture prior, written before the call", *extra)

    n_before = counts("search_executions")

           and counts("search_executions") == n_before, f"rc={r.returncode} {(r.stdout + r.stderr)[-200:]}")
    r = ls_bare("unknown parameter", "--parameter", "999999")

           r.returncode != 0 and "has no matching row in" in (r.stdout + r.stderr)
           and counts("search_executions") == n_before, f"rc={r.returncode} {(r.stdout + r.stderr)[-200:]}")
    r = ls_bare("parameter only", "--parameter", str(PARAM))
    row = q("SELECT slug, parameter_id FROM search_executions WHERE query_text=?", "fixture N: parameter only")
    record("N03", "a search naming only a parameter is stored with a NULL slug",
           r.returncode == 0 and row == [(None, PARAM)], f"rc={r.returncode} {r.stderr[-200:]} {row}")

        return run_cli("add-candidate", "--exec-id", str(exec_id), "--disposition", "PENDING-VERIFICATION",
                       "--title", "fixture N candidate", "--surfaced-in", "transcripts/README.md",
                       "--surfaced-quote", "single home for what the agents actually did", "--session", S, *extra)

    (ex_slug,) = q("SELECT exec_id FROM search_executions WHERE query_text=?", "fixture M: live codes")[0]
    c_before = counts("search_candidates")

    refused_ok = (r_no.returncode != 0 and "found_under_slug is required" in (r_no.stdout + r_no.stderr)
                  and r_bad.returncode != 0 and "is not in `slugs`" in (r_bad.stdout + r_bad.stderr)

def unretire(con, spec):
    """Make a retired specification live again. A live stated or provisional row must carry a
    marker (migration 116); the weakest band is legal on any such row. `reretire` undoes it."""
    con.execute("UPDATE specifications SET retired_at=NULL, marker=CASE WHEN state IN "
                "('stated','provisional') THEN ? END WHERE specification_id=?",
                (EvidenceMarker.WEAK.value, spec))

def reretire(spec, at=None, by=None, why=None):
    """Put a specification back as the canonical copy held it: retired, and unmarked (a retired
    row is exempt from the marker CHECK, and `unretire` gave it one)."""
    con = sqlite3.connect(DB)
    if at is None:
        con.execute("UPDATE specifications SET marker=NULL WHERE specification_id=?", (spec,))
    else:
        con.execute("UPDATE specifications SET retired_at=?, retired_by_session=?, "
                    "retirement_reason=?, marker=NULL WHERE specification_id=?", (at, by, why, spec))
    con.commit()
    con.close()

def refusal(fn, *a, **k):
    """The Refusal's text if `fn` refuses, else None.

    Any OTHER exception is a defect, not a refusal, and must never count as one: it is
    printed and returns None, so the assertion that expected a refusal goes red and the
    run carries on to the cases after it (fault injection showed a crash here hiding
    every later case)."""
    try:
        fn(*a, **k)
    except Refusal as exc:
        return str(exc)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- reported, never swallowed as a pass
        print(f"      DEFECT, not a refusal: {exc.__class__.__name__}: {exc}")
    return None


def q(sql, *params):

def w(sql, *params):

    con = sqlite3.connect(DB)

    finally:

"""A fixture retrieval-log root that a pre-admission fetch cannot reach (T-073).

A batch persists what it fetched under the id its source will take BEFORE `db.py add-source` admits the source, so between
the two the retrieval log holds an id the database does not. A fixture that mints a source through the writer takes the
database's next id, which is that folder's id, and inherits the saved text: a refusal case then goes red for a reason that
has nothing to do with what it tests. The fix is to isolate the ROOT, not to change the id: a real admission must still take
the id its folder was filed under.

`fixture_log_root(dest, db_path)` symlinks into `dest` each folder of the repository's retrieval log EXCEPT a folder whose
manifest names a ref_id above the high-water mark of the database at `db_path`; such a folder is linked file by file with
only the lines and artefacts of those ids left out, and one line is printed for each.
"""
import json
import pathlib
import re
import sqlite3
import sys

REPO = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "scripts"))
import dbcore  # noqa: E402


def fixture_log_root(dest, db_path, source=None):
    dest, source = pathlib.Path(dest), pathlib.Path(source or REPO / "retrieval-log")
    dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    ro = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db_path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    try:
        high = dbcore.ref_id_high_water(ro)
    finally:
        ro.close()
    for d in sorted(source.iterdir()):
        if not d.is_dir():
            continue
        manifest = d / "manifest.jsonl"
        keep, ahead, stems = [], set(), set()
        if manifest.exists():
            for line in manifest.open(encoding="utf-8"):
                if not line.strip():
                    continue
                rec = json.loads(line)
                ref = (rec.get("ref_id") or "").strip()
                m = dbcore._MINTABLE.fullmatch(ref)
                if m and int(m.group(1)) > high:
                    ahead.add(ref)
                    if rec.get("artefact"):
                        stems.add(pathlib.Path(rec["artefact"]).stem)
                else:
                    keep.append(line)
        if not ahead:
            link = dest / d.name
            if not link.exists():
                link.symlink_to(d.resolve())
            continue
        # A batch files several sources into one folder and admits them one at a time: leave out only the lines (and the
        # files) of the ids above the mark, not the artefacts of the sources already admitted (T-073 critic, 2026-11-15).
        print(f"fixture root: left out {sorted(ahead)} from {d.name} (above the copy's high-water mark {high})")
        out = dest / d.name
        out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        (out / "manifest.jsonl").write_text("".join(keep), encoding="utf-8")

    The identity lens counts through `parent_code` (a parent's cell gathers its descendants' figures, a child's only

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/audit/translation_pointer_audit.py -- every current translation still translates the cell it points at.

WHAT WRONG THING REACHES THE GUIDEBOOK WITHOUT IT (T-049): a translation shown beside a quotation it no longer
translates. SQLite cannot hold a foreign key to "any cell", so `translations.source_*` is a pointer nothing else
enforces, and `source_sha256` is how a change to the original is seen.

For every CURRENT translation (status translated or reviewed, not retired) it checks that
  * the pointer resolves to a text cell today (`dbcore.read_cell`, the one rule the verbs use);
  * the cell's hash is the one recorded when it was translated;
  * the translation states the original's numbers and no others (`db.translation_number_gaps`, the rule
    `db.py record-translation` applies at write time).
Prints `EXAMINED: <n>`, the current translations. Zero until the first translation is recorded.

Usage:  python3 scripts/audit/translation_pointer_audit.py
Exit 0 every current translation holds; 1 one does not; 2 cannot run.
"""
import os
import sqlite3
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "scripts"))
import dbcore                                                          # noqa: E402
import db                                                              # noqa: E402

DB_PATH = Path(os.environ.get("GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH", REPO / "data" / "guidebook.db"))


def main():
    if not DB_PATH.exists():
        print(f"translation_pointer_audit: no database at {DB_PATH}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{DB_PATH}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    try:
        if not conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE name='translations'").fetchone():
            print("translation_pointer_audit: the translations table is absent", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        rows = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM v_translations_current ORDER BY translation_id").fetchall()
        bad = []
        for r in rows:
            tid, where = r["translation_id"], (r["source_table"], r["source_column"], r["source_row_key"])
            original, _, why = dbcore.read_cell(conn, *where)
            if why:
                bad.append(f"translation {tid}: the pointer does not resolve: {why}")
            elif db.translation_sha256(original) != r["source_sha256"]:
                bad.append(f"translation {tid}: the original at {where[0]}.{where[1]} [{where[2]}] "
                           f"has changed since it was translated")
            else:
                dropped, added = db.translation_number_gaps(original, r["translated_text"],
                                                            db.translation_claimed_value(conn, *where))
                if dropped or added:
                    bad.append(f"translation {tid}: numbers dropped {dropped or 'none'}, added {added or 'none'}")
    finally:
        conn.close()
    print("translation_pointer_audit -- every current translation still translates the cell it points at")
    print(f"EXAMINED: {len(rows)}")

--    the justification absorbed into the base's own columns; no foreign key, nothing read from the evidence stage.
--    The writer (db._kind_refusal) refuses a quote that holds no digit (any script's digits, so the CHECK below does
--    not repeat that test with an ASCII class). WHETHER THE BASE SHOULD REPEAT A SOURCE'S QUOTED WORDS IS STILL THE
--    OWNER'S QUESTION: OD-71's "What it does not decide" leaves it open; the coordinator chose to keep the words so
--    the refusal T-020 built is not lost, and the owner may reverse that.
-- 2. ALL OR NONE. A kind, its quote, its URL and a page or a clause are present together or absent together; a
--    locator part, a line, a ref_id or a quote with no kind is refused.
-- 3. HOLES CLOSED, as 154 closed them on source_clauses: a cell holding only whitespace is blank by 154's character set
--    (no-break space and the Unicode spaces included) plus the zero-width characters U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+2060
--    and U+FEFF (dbcore.ZERO_WIDTH holds the same five; a test compares the two); a zero-width character anywhere in a
